jan the peak of paradise

⭐ absolute peak season

january is as good as it gets in palawan. the dry season is fully in charge, the skies are blue every single day, the sea is glass calm and the lagoons of el nido are so clear you can see straight to the bottom. this is peak season and for very good reason. island hopping in coron, the castaway experience on daracotan island, snorkelling with turtles — all of it is at its most magical in january. book early because everyone knows about this month.

☀️
avg high
31°c
warm year round
💧
rainfall
15mm
dry and barely any
🌊
sea temp
28°c
flat and perfect

✓ what's great

  • blue skies every single day with zero rain
  • the sea is impossibly calm and clear for island hopping
  • el nido lagoons at their absolute clearest
  • the castaway experience is pure paradise
  • turtles are reliably spotted snorkelling in palawan

📌 things to note

  • peak season so popular spots get busier
  • accommodation fills up months in advance
  • prices are at their highest of the year

🎉 festivals & events

jan
ati-atihan festivalone of the philippines most colourful and wild festivals in kalibo, aklan. street dancing, tribal costumes and music for days. completely unmissable if you can catch it.
jan
sinulog festivalthe huge cebu city festival with some of the most spectacular street processions in all of southeast asia. worth extending your trip for.
🍗
must-try dish
adobo

the unofficial national dish — chicken or pork braised in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic and bay leaves until deeply sticky and tender. every family makes it differently and every version is their grandmother's recipe. wherever and whenever you visit, this is the dish you'll eat.

every home, every carinderia, every turo-turo. everywhere.

feb genuinely flawless

⭐ the best single month

february might be the most perfect month in the philippines. rainfall drops to its absolute minimum, the trade winds keep things breezy and comfortable rather than hot and sticky, and the visibility underwater for snorkelling is at its best of the entire year. the el nido lagoons in february look like something out of a screensaver except they are real and you are actually floating in them. if you are a beach person, a snorkelling person, or just a person who loves perfection, go in february.

  • island hopping conditions genuinely perfect

📌 things to note

  • very popular so book well ahead
  • flights to palawan can be expensive in this window
  • peak season pricing across the board

valentines in the philippinesfilipinos absolutely love valentines day and the whole country goes full romantic. beach dinners, floating candles and incredible sunsets. honestly a brilliant time to be there.

mar hot and heavenly

⭐ still brilliant dry season

march is the hottest month in the philippines and also one of the most spectacular. the dry season is still going strong, the beaches are stunning, and the sea is the warmest it gets all year. it does get very hot especially inland so you will want to spend as much time as possible on the water which honestly is not exactly a hardship when the water looks like this. el nido and coron are at their finest and the sunsets in march are something else entirely. a brilliant month to go.

  • warmest sea temperatures of the year
  • el nido and coron in stunning condition
  • incredible sunsets throughout march

📌 things to note

  • hottest month so inland can be intense
  • pack light breathable clothing and high spf
  • some sites close for holy week

apr holy week and sunshine

⭐ brilliant with great festivals

april is the hottest month of the year in the philippines and it is genuinely stunning. the dry season is in its final glorious stretch and every beach looks incredible. the el nido lagoons, the coron shipwrecks, the daracotan castaway experience — everything is operating at peak beauty. holy week brings this incredible cultural energy to the entire country with processions and ceremonies everywhere. it is hot though, so stay hydrated, wear factor 50, and spend as much time in the sea as humanly possible.

  • every beach and lagoon looking incredible

📌 things to note

  • the hottest month of the year, bring factor 50
  • some businesses close for holy week
  • rains can start appearing late in the month

may transition time

🌤 dry season ending

may is the transition month between the dry and wet seasons and it is actually still very good for most of the trip. you will get mostly sunny days with some afternoon showers building. the sea is still beautifully warm, the lagoons are still gorgeous, and island hopping is still completely feasible and enjoyable. prices start to drop too as the peak season winds down. pack a light rain jacket for afternoon showers but do not let it put you off. may is still a cracking time to visit the philippines.

  • still mostly sunny with warm seas
  • prices starting to drop from peak season
  • afternoon showers are warm and dramatic not miserable
  • island hopping still completely feasible
  • much quieter than january through april

📌 things to note

  • showers building throughout the month
  • some days might have disrupted outdoor plans
  • sea can get choppier in the second half of may

jun rainy season begins

🌧 wet season starting

june marks the start of the south-west monsoon in the philippines and things do get noticeably wetter. however we want to be honest with you rather than pretend otherwise. island hopping becomes less reliable in june and the boat trips around el nido and coron can be affected by rougher seas. that said the rain is warm, the landscapes turn an extraordinary green, prices are at their most affordable and the cultural experiences on the tour are completely unaffected. if you are flexible and a good sport about the rain it is genuinely still a great trip.

  • lowest prices of the year
  • virtually no crowds anywhere
  • landscapes turn an incredible vivid green
  • cooking class and village experiences completely unaffected
  • you will have beaches almost entirely to yourself

📌 things to note

  • rainy season with heavy afternoon and evening showers
  • island hopping can be affected by rough seas
  • some boat tours may be cancelled on bad weather days
  • pack a proper waterproof and embrace it

jul peak monsoon month

🌧 full monsoon season

july is the peak of the south-west monsoon and we want to be upfront with you. it rains a lot and island hopping can be significantly disrupted. boat trips around el nido and coron are subject to weather cancellations and some days will be spent on land rather than the water. the cultural experiences, the cooking class, the village visit and the city time in manila are all brilliant regardless. if the water-based activities are the main reason you are going, july is not the month we would recommend. but if you are on a tight budget and love having places completely to yourself, july has a certain magic.

  • island hopping regularly disrupted or cancelled

aug still monsoon but easing

🌧 monsoon easing slowly

august is still firmly in the monsoon season but conditions are very gradually starting to ease compared to july. you will still get significant rain and island hopping remains subject to weather but there are more sunny windows appearing throughout the month. the undisputed highlight of august is the kadayawan festival in davao which is one of the most spectacular and colourful events in the entire philippines. the cultural triangle of our tour is still completely brilliant and prices remain very low. september and much better weather is just around the corner.

sep things start improving

🌤 improving but still variable

september is when the philippines starts to shake off the monsoon and conditions noticeably improve week on week. you will still get some rain and the odd disrupted boat day but there are increasingly long sunny stretches especially in the second half of the month. prices are still well below peak, the crowds are nowhere near, and by late september the lagoons and beaches are looking really beautiful again. it is a genuinely interesting time to visit — you get the affordability of the wet season with the beginning of the good weather returning.

oct shoulder season gem

👍 conditions rapidly improving

october is a genuinely brilliant month to visit the philippines and most people do not realise it. conditions are improving rapidly every single week and by late october the sea is calming beautifully, the lagoons are clearing back to that impossible blue, and island hopping is largely back on the table. prices are still noticeably lower than peak season and crowds are minimal. you are essentially getting november conditions at shoulder season prices. our october gals consistently have amazing trips. it is a proper hidden gem month.

nov our insider tip month

⭐ great weather without peak prices

november is our absolute insider tip month for the philippines. the dry season has officially arrived, the sea is calming down beautifully, the el nido lagoons are clearing back to that electric blue, and the weather is reliably gorgeous. but the peak season crowds have not arrived yet and prices are significantly lower than december through april. you essentially get the same incredible experience as the peak months without paying peak prices or competing with as many tourists. our november gals consistently rave about this month and we completely understand why.

dec peak paradise season

⭐ peak season at its finest

december in the philippines is genuinely one of the most magical places on earth. the dry season is in full swing, the skies are blue and reliable, the sea is flat calm and crystal clear, and the filipino love of christmas turns the entire country into this extraordinary display of lights, music and warmth. filipinos start celebrating christmas in september so by december it has reached full magnificent fever pitch. el nido by day is stunning. the sunsets over coron are the most spectacular of the year. and the castaway experience on daracotan island in december is pure undiluted paradise. book very early.

  • sea is crystal clear and completely calm
  • the most magical christmas atmosphere of anywhere in asia
  • el nido lagoons at their sparkling best
  • castaway island experience is pure paradise in december

📌 things to note

  • the busiest and most expensive month

simbang gabinine nights of pre-dawn mass that filipinos absolutely love. the churches glow with candlelight and the streets fill with food stalls serving traditional christmas treats.

christmas in the philippinesfilipinos celebrate christmas harder than almost anywhere else on earth. the whole country is decorated, joyful and incredibly welcoming. it is extraordinary to be part of it.
🍗
must-try dish
adobo

the unofficial national dish — chicken or pork braised in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic and bay leaves until deeply sticky and tender. every family makes it differently and every version is their grandmother's recipe. wherever and whenever you visit, this is the dish you'll eat.

every home, every carinderia, every turo-turo. everywhere.
🗣️
phrase to learn before you go
tagalog
saan ang comfort room?
where is the bathroom?
say it: sah-an ang com-fort room
essential. filipinos call it the comfort room, not the bathroom. knowing this will save you considerable confusion
📱
staying connected
esim

grab an esim before you fly — apps like airalo or holafly let you land with data already switched on, no sim-swapping or airport queues needed. coverage is solid in el nido and coron themselves, just patchy on some of the boat crossings in between.

download it while you still have wifi — most esims need an internet connection to activate.

destination overview

when to visit the philippines

the philippines is one of the most weather-dependent destinations we run trips to, and we want to be genuinely honest with you about it. the dry season from november through april is when the island hopping in palawan is at its absolute dreamy best. the wet season from june through october brings real rain and can disrupt boat trips. but the cultural experiences, cooking classes and village visits are brilliant in any month, and the wet season does come with the lowest prices and the emptiest beaches you will ever see.

our gwt philippines tour is built around palawan, which has its own microclimate that is slightly drier than other parts of the country. use this guide to find your perfect month, then see the full 10-day itinerary →

✈️ gwt insider tip

our recommendation

november and february are our two favourite months to send the gals to the philippines. february for the absolute peak of perfection. november for the same incredible experience without paying january prices or fighting for space on the beaches. both months will genuinely blow your mind.

faqs

got questions?

what is the best time to visit the philippines?

the best time to visit the philippines for island hopping in palawan is november through april during the dry season. january and february are the peak months with the lowest rainfall, calmest seas and best snorkelling visibility.

what is the philippines like in june?

june marks the start of the south-west monsoon in the philippines. island hopping can be affected by rougher seas but cultural experiences remain brilliant. prices are at their most affordable and crowds are minimal.

what is the philippines like in december?

december is peak season in the philippines. dry season, crystal clear seas, blue skies every day. the philippines has the most magical christmas atmosphere in asia with decorations, music and celebrations from december through the new year.

is november a good time to visit the philippines?

november is an excellent time to visit the philippines. the dry season has returned, seas are calm and clear, and conditions are comparable to peak season but without peak prices or peak crowds.

what is the rainy season in the philippines?

the rainy season in the philippines runs roughly june through october, with july and august being the wettest months. the south-west monsoon brings heavy rain to palawan during this period. island hopping can be disrupted but cultural experiences remain excellent.
